riverbend-music-center.sensory.2: Riverbend Music Center and PNC Pavilion offer sign language interpretation upon request. Requests for sign language interpreting services must be received no later than 3 weeks before the event, and are subject to the availability of an interpreter. Please email info@riverbend.org to request an interpreter.
riverbend-music-center.cognitive.1:
Parking is included in the price of each ticket and is available for all ticketholders of Riverbend Music Center and PNC Pavilion events. Parking is available in surrounding lots by entering Gate 1, Gate 2 and Gate 4.
Parking lots open 2 hours before Door Time unless otherwise specified.
Please check the event page of your event for more information.
riverbend-music-center.cognitive.2: If you are in need of further assistance, please call 513.232.5882
riverbend-music-center.mobility.5: Chairs in the ADA areas have the following measurements: 33 ½ inches tall, 18 in wide and 17 from front to back of the seat.
riverbend-music-center.chronic.2: All events are rain or shine, and no refunds or exchanges will be issued in the event of rain. In the event of severe weather during a concert, alerts and instructions will be given via the venue social media pages.
great-american-ball-park.mobility.2:
Accessible seating is located in the last rows of Infield Box, Field Box, Terrace Line, Terrace Outfield, Mezzanine, Outer Mezzanine and View Level Box. The top accessible row of each section does have electrical outlets available for use.
All ADA seating is accessible by elevators and ramps.

The majority of Great American Ball Park Entrances are on accessible routes. Gates A, B, C, and H are at street level, while Gates D and E are on the Suite Level. Gate D is accessible to Suite Holders only and can be accessed by ramp, elevator, or escalator. Gate E is accessible to all Guests by ramp, elevator, or escalator.
great-american-ball-park.sensory.1: Guests can request the use of Assisted Listening Devices (ALD) at any TriHealth Fan Accommodation Station located behind Sections 119 or 420.

The Cincinnati Reds provide two dedicated captioning boards to provide a readily accessible experience for patrons of Great American Ball Park who are deaf, hard of hearing or late deafened. The dimensions of the dedicated left-field captioning board are 3.1 feet x 22 feet with a font size of one foot per each of its two lines of text. In order to provide captioning to patrons seated in the outfield sections of the ballpark, the Reds have also added a dedicated captioning board along the first-base line of the ballpark. The dimensions of the first base captioning board are 3.1 feet x 17 feet with a font size that is also one foot per each of its two lines of text. In addition to in-bowl captioning, the Reds will caption the game broadcasts in all club areas of the ballpark through closed captioning on televisions dispersed throughout the club areas.
great-american-ball-park.mobility.3: Guests in need of a wheelchair transport can make their request to the nearest Reds Public Safety Employee, either of the two TriHealth Fan Accommodation Stations located at Sections 119 and 420 near Gapper's Alley, or at any of the TriHealth First Aid Stations located near Sections 109, 127 or 409. A Game Day Team member will escort you to your seat and can pick you up when you are ready to leave. Wheelchairs are not available for personal use during the event.
great-american-ball-park.sensory.2: Fans needing assistance at Reds games can download the Aira Explorer app to access visual interpreting, or the Aira ASL app for American Sign Language interpreting.

As part of the TriHealth Family Zone, fans will have access to a sensory room, a therapeutic space with a variety of equipment that provides individuals with special needs a safe location with personalized sensory input and is staffed by TriHealth Medical Personnel.
great-american-ball-park.mobility.4: Elevators can be found behind Sections 101, 110, 121, 127 and 135.

Accessible parking is available in the East section of the Central Riverfront Garage (formerly called the Great American Ball Park Parking Garage) for $27 and in the East Garage for $16. While the number of accessible parking spaces is more than adequate, guests are still encouraged to arrive at the scheduled gate opening time to make it more convenient to the accessible parking spaces. These areas are pay-upon-entry and will be Credit Card ONLY. Parking will be sold on a first come, first served basis, based on availability. The Great American Ball Park parking lots open 5 hours before game time.
paycor-stadium.mobility.1: Accessible (ADA) seating is available throughout Paycor Stadium, on all three levels. Guests who require ADA seating should contact the Bengals ticket office at 513-621-8383 to purchase those seats in advance. Seats are offered on a first come, first served basis.
paycor-stadium.cognitive.1: Due to traffic congestion on Central Avenue, the road will be closed until 30 minutes after the event. Pick up of guests after the event may begin once Central Avenue is reopened.
paycor-stadium.mobility.3: Elevators are reserved for use by guests with mobility needs (along with one companion) as well as suite holders and club seat patrons. Elevators are located on the East and West sides of Paycor Stadium.
paycor-stadium.mobility.4: There are seven entry gates. All entrances are accessible for guests with disabilities.
paycor-stadium.chronic.2: An exception will be made for medically necessary items after proper inspection at the gate. Diapers and wipes can be carried in a clear bag, however, non-clear diaper bags are
paycor-stadium.chronic.3: Sealed bottled water is permitted, but food is prohibited (only exception is for medical/dietary conditions)
paycor-stadium.cognitive.2: In accordance with Federal ADA Guidelines, certified service animals assisting guests with disabilities are permitted inside Paycor Stadium. Emotional support animals and comfort animals are not permitted in Paycor Stadium. Under the ADA, service animals must be harnessed, leashed, or tethered, unless the individual's disability prevents using these devices or these devices interfere with the service animal's safe, effective performance of tasks. In that case, the individual must maintain control of the animal through voice, signal, or other effective controls. The handler is responsible for the service animal at all times, including any necessary clean up. To relieve the animal, the handler should contact a stadium gate manager to obtain permission prior to exiting the stadium to ensure they will be granted re-entry.
paycor-stadium.mobility.5: Accessible Parking: Every lot provides handicap parking spaces for season ticket holders with passes for the lot.
